question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 2-week NQ minus ES return spreads. Median near 0 with a slight positive tech drift. The regime is high-volatility: the Nasdaq fell 3.4% vs the S&P's 2.7% in the week of Nov 2-6 on post-midterm AI-regulation fears, VIX is 25.6, and Nvidia reports Nov 17 inside the window. The spread tracks market direction (NQ beta ~1.2), so a rebound or a deeper rout pushes it either way; I see no reliable directional edge, so the distribution is symmetric and wide. Escape past +/-5pp would need a ~3-SD tech-specific shock; I priced ~1.5% on each side. Market check: no Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi contract found.

calls.reasoning: The reference class is 2-week NQ-ES total price-return spreads. They center near zero with a small positive drift from NQ's higher beta (~1.2). The regime now is high-volatility and tech-specific. In the week of Nov 2-6 the Nasdaq Composite fell 3.4% vs 2.7% for the S&P on fears of post-midterm AI regulation. Single-day gaps reached about 1.1pp (Nov 5) in both directions. Nvidia reports Nov 17, inside the window. Direction has no reliable edge: a continued chip rebound or a strong NVDA print favors NQ, while more regulation headlines or higher yields favor ES. So the median sits slightly above 0 and the spread is widened. Market check: no Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmaker contract found by the runs. I did no web retrieval myself on this run.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: P0 is the Nov 6 close and P1 the Nov 20 close on Yahoo NQ=F/ES=F; Nasdaq Comp fell 3.37% vs S&P 2.68% for the week; Nov 6 was a partial tech rebound; NVDA reports Nov 17. Run 2 says Nov 5 was -5.5%/-4.4%. The other runs don't contradict that, but it isn't independently verified, and it doesn't change the forecast materially. The remaining disagreement is judgment about dispersion: implied 90-10 widths of 4.1-4.75pp. Run 3 derives a normal-regime 2-week SD of 1.4-1.6pp, which looks too high: calm-regime evidence points to about 1.0-1.3. The current elevated regime justifies scaling up to about 1.6pp. I adopt about 4.2pp, close to Runs 1 and 2. No evidence supports a directional tilt beyond the small beta drift, so the median is about +0.08. I price small tail escape mass (1% each side) because a ±5pp spread is about 3 SD and needs a tech-specific crash or melt-up. That is possible in this regime but rare.
